story: At the Sumter Oaks Rec Center on Tuesday evening, Gary is content and promising Hal a Saturday night plan with freshly wiped boots, while Donna, upbeat as ever, coaxes one last rally out of Gary with her dinks on court one. Hal is heading out along Magnolia Loop, cart keys jingling as he goes. Over at her house, Rosa is determined, going through her pantry and fridge against her grocery list and marking what she still needs to buy.
events: Donna (pickleball court 1): Pick up my paddle and rally one last time with Gary, working on his dinks
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Go through the pantry and fridge against my grocery list and mark what I still need to buy

gary.thought_process: Hal just told me dinner at Rosa's is Saturday at six, and Donna says we're wrapping up and walking over together. I already told Hal I'd head over after one more rally, so I shouldn't repeat myself. My cart form is filed, I've kept my word, and being counted on feels good. Best move now is to acknowledge Hal's boots-and-on-time reminder briefly and get moving with them rather than stand around chatting.

parameters.content: Saturday at six, boots wiped, I've got it written down this time. Let me stash my paddle and I'll walk out with you two.

donna.thought_process: Gary and Hal both just spoke and Gary asked for one more rally before heading to Rosa's. I already told Hal we'd all walk over together, so I shouldn't repeat that. I signed Pruitt-Kowalski on the ladder earlier, but I haven't checked the standings. Since the court is reserved and Gary wants one more rally, the best forward step is to actually play it and keep building his dink, since that's what gets us climbing the ladder.

parameters.content: Pick up my paddle and rally one last time with Gary, working on his dinks

hal.thought_process: Gary and Donna already said they're wrapping up and will walk over to Rosa's with me. I told Gary about the dinner last tick and he's keeping his word. Nagging them again would just be repeating myself. The complaints about the cart and the flamingos are settled, so there's nothing left to report. Best move is to head out toward Magnolia Loop, let them finish their rally, and be there when they catch up. Might as well make sure I'm on time for Rosa's.

parameters.content: Heading out toward Rosa's so we're not late; Gary and Donna can catch up when they've finished their rally.

rosa.thought_process: I've already pulled out the tablecloth, set the platters, drafted the menu and grocery list, and checked the shift schedule twice. Everything is confirmed for Saturday at six with Hal, Donna, and Gary. Nobody's around to talk to, and re-checking the schedule a third time would just be fussing. The one real step left is the borrow list: I need extra chairs, and I should look at what's actually in my kitchen before I commit to the grocery run. Time to move the plan forward by working through the menu and ingredients in the kitchen.

parameters.content: Go through the pantry and fridge against my grocery list and mark what I still need to buy

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
